summary: A governed intelligence layer for fragmented government records.
editor_note: Government data is not scarce; it is trapped in scanned PDFs, maps, and incompatible databases. Apaluma connects records around places, permits, facilities, and enforcement history, then gives agencies role-based search, mapping, permitting, and incident response. Unlike a rip-and-replace records project, the bet is an intelligence layer over legacy systems. The question is whether deployments stay repeatable across agencies with different ontologies, procurement rules, and data quality.

product_evidence.claim: Apaluma says its Fathom layer ingests scanned PDFs and structured records, applies OCR and classification, and connects facilities, permits, violations, and locations through an agency-specific ontology.
The official site exposes separate Harbor permitting, Riptide incident-response, and Meridian cross-jurisdiction mapping workflows with role-based access and audit controls.
Apaluma presents an API-first integration approach intended to connect legacy systems instead of requiring agencies to replace them.

market_context.primary_user: Government analysts, regulators, permitting teams, incident responders, and records staff.
market_context.differentiation: Apaluma connects decades of regulatory records to physical places and agency workflows while preserving role-based governance and existing systems.
market_context.why_now: Agencies are under pressure to answer permitting, environmental, enforcement, and public-record questions faster as document understanding and geospatial linking become practical.

risks.claim: The falsifiable risk is whether Apaluma can make agency deployments repeatable when each jurisdiction has different source systems, ontologies, procurement rules, and record quality.
risks.basis: VentureDex assessment from the official integration and agency-workflow claims; deployment-speed and FOIA outcome claims were not independently benchmarked.

risks.claim: The announcement names Crosslink Capital and Kickstart as joint leads and Haven Ventures and Overwater Ventures as co-leads; the lead field preserves the first named joint-lead pair.
